text:
Maya (acme-corp): hey support — since yesterday our prod calls to redwood-xl have been returning 500s and high latency right after a canary rollout. one example request id from our client logs: rq_3b5f7a4e-9c2. curl we used returns 500 quickly. can you repro and advise if we should pin to stable?

Jules (support): thanks Maya. can you paste the full request_id/response body + the approximate timestamp? also can you run a repro with verbose curl so we get headers?

Maya (acme-corp): full request id: rq_3b5f7a4e-9c2, timestamp ~1718456710 (UTC). response body: "{\"error\":\"internal_server_error\",\"code\":500}\". our curl repro (what we ran):
```
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-xl","input":"hello world"}' \
  --max-time 15
```
we also tried with our app sending X-Request-Id: rq_3b5f7a4e-9c2. we think we had been pinned to redwood-xl@v1.2.3 but we didn't change anything right before the failure.

deploy-bot: canary rollout redwood-xl@v1.3 started by @Aria at 2024-06-30T12:45Z (rollout id: rl_89d).

Aria (oncall-eng): i'm on it. i'll attempt a repro from our staging with same headers. @Samir can you tail inference node logs for rq_3b5f7a4e-9c2? initial hunch: KV cache invalidation or a kernel regression on the canary.

Samir (infra): tailing logs now. saw entries for rq_3b5f7a4e-9c2: 
```
[1718456710.112] INFO Dispatch: received request rq_3b5f7a4e-9c2 route=customer-acme shard=g-12
[1718456711.504] ERROR DispatchTimeout: shard busy (timeout=10s) rq=rq_3b5f7a4e-9c2
[1718456711.505] WARN Routing: attempted fallback to model redwood-xl-small@stable for rq_3b5f7a4e-9c2
[1718456711.506] ERROR KernelFailure: kernel oom on node g-12 canary-build=2024-06-29-ngx
[1718456711.507] ERROR Response: failed to serve rq_3b5f7a4e-9c2 -> 500
```
looks like the request tried to fallback but the fallback path also errored in this case (kernel oom then generic 500). i also see GC spikes on g-12 around the timeframe.

Jules (support): ok — we'll need a debug bundle with traces (router decisions, model hashes, node metrics). maya can you upload the debug bundle from your side (client-side headers + body) or allow us to grab the server-side trace? i'll create an internal debug ticket.

Aria (oncall-eng): repro steps i ran from our side:
```
# reproduce with X-Request-Id header
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Request-Id: rq_3b5f7a4e-9c2" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-xl@v1.3-canary","input":"hello world"}' \
  --max-time 20
```
result: 502/timeout after ~11s from canary build. server logs match Samir's: kernel oom -> dispatch timeout -> 500. when i forced a model pin to stable (v1.2.3) via admin API the same request returned 200 in ~180ms. example pin command: 
```
# pin deployment to a specific model version (admin-only)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/deployments/<deployment_id>/pin \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model_version":"v1.2.3"}'
```
or via console: Models > redwood-xl > Pin version v1.2.3 for route customer-acme.

Aria (oncall-eng): notes on fallback behavior: our router will attempt to route to a compatible fallback model if the primary is overloaded or fails (e.g., redwood-xl -> redwood-xl-small@stable). in this incident the fallback attempted but the node-level kernel oom prevented a clean fallback series, which resulted in a 500. pinning to v1.2.3 avoids the canary kernels that trigger the oom.

Maya (acme-corp): please pin us to stable asap — we need production healthy. also please share debug bundle link so we can view traces on our side.

Jules (support): received. i'm creating debug bundle now and will attach the server-side trace + routing decisions. @Aria can you perform an immediate mitigation (pin customer route) and follow up with rollback plan? 

Aria (oncall-eng): done — pinned customer-acme route to redwood-xl@v1.2.3 at 1718456950. opened INC-2345 for tracking. monitoring shows p95 latency dropped back to normal within 2m. will rollback or re-run canary only after kernel patch. created debug bundle and uploaded: https://s3.internal.redwood/debug/1718456789-rq_3b5f7a4e.zip (contains traces, node metrics, routing decisions).

Maya (acme-corp): confirmed — errors cleared and latency down. thanks. any action for us?

Samir (infra): we'll investigate kernel build causing OOMs and schedule a canary hold. please don't re-enable canary traffic for 24h. we'll post a postmortem with repro, root cause, and remedial steps (INC-2345).

Jules (support): noted. next steps for support: follow up with customer when postmortem is ready, confirm billing unaffected (billing-bot please sanity check if any surge credits needed). :thumbsup:

billing-bot: no abnormal billing spikes detected for customer-acme in the affected window.

Jules (support): thanks everyone. i'll keep this thread open until postmortem posted. if you (Maya) need anything else to repro on your side (extra logs, curl with headers, or a temporary pin change) ping here. :pray:
